note.explanation: Motion is classified by how a body moves: it may move as a whole, turn around an axis, or move to and fro around a fixed position.
note.simple: Look at the path or movement: straight, irregular, circular, turning around an axis, or to and fro.
note.checkQuestion: What type of motion does an electric fan show?
note.title: Recognising types of motion
steps: If every particle moves in the same direction, identify translatory motion and then check whether its path is straight, irregular, or circular.
If points of the body move around a fixed axis, identify rotatory motion.
If the body repeats a to-and-fro movement about a fixed position, identify vibratory motion.
note.answer: The three general types are translatory, rotatory, and vibratory motion.

mcqs.stem: A freely falling body is an example of:
rationales: Correct: a freely falling body moves along a straight line, so its motion is linear.
Incorrect: random motion follows an irregular path.
Incorrect: circular motion follows a circle.
Incorrect: vibratory motion is repeated to-and-fro motion about a fixed position.

mcqs.stem: A bee moving along an irregular path shows:
rationales: Incorrect: translatory motion requires every particle to move uniformly in the same direction.
Incorrect: rotatory motion is movement around a fixed point or axis.
Incorrect: vibratory motion repeats to and fro about a fixed position.
Correct: movement along an irregular path is random motion.

mcqs.stem: A Ferris wheel is an example of:
rationales: Incorrect: linear motion is along a straight line.
Correct: a Ferris wheel moves along a circular path.
Incorrect: rotatory motion is when each point of a body moves around a fixed point or axis.
Incorrect: vibratory motion is repeated to-and-fro motion about a fixed position.

mcqs.stem: The motion of an electric fan is:
rationales: Incorrect: translatory motion describes a body moving in the same direction, rather than turning around an axis.
Correct: points of the fan move around its fixed axis, so its motion is rotatory.
Incorrect: linear motion is movement along a straight line.
Incorrect: random motion follows an irregular path.

mcqs.stem: A swing repeatedly moving to and fro about its fixed position shows:
rationales: Incorrect: rotatory motion is movement around an axis.
Incorrect: circular motion is movement along a circle.
Correct: repeated to-and-fro motion about a fixed position is vibratory motion.
Incorrect: linear motion is movement along a straight line.

written.text: Describe different types of motion. Also give examples.
written.finalAnswer: There are three general types of motion: translatory, rotatory and vibratory. Translatory motion occurs when every particle of a body moves uniformly in the same direction; a train or car is an example. Its types include linear motion, such as a freely falling body; random motion, such as a bee moving along an irregular path; and circular motion, such as a Ferris wheel. Rotatory motion occurs when each point of a body moves around a fixed point (axis); an electric fan or a top is an example. Vibratory motion is repeated to-and-fro motion about a fixed position; a swing is an example.

modelAnswer: There are three general types of motion: translatory, rotatory and vibratory.
If every particle of a body moves uniformly in the same direction, it is called translatory motion; the motion of a train or a car is an example.
Translatory motion can be linear, random or circular: a freely falling body is linear, a bee moving along an irregular path is random, and a Ferris wheel is circular.
If each point of a body moves around a fixed point (axis), the motion is called rotatory motion; an electric fan or a top is an example.
When a body repeats its to and fro motion about a fixed position, the motion is called vibratory motion; a swing is an example.

For translatory motion, remember to name its three types—linear, random, and circular—and provide an example of each if space allows.

explain.title: The three general types
explain.body: Generally, there are three types of motion of bodies: translatory motion, rotatory motion, and vibratory motion.

explain.title: Translatory motion and its types
explain.body: “If the motion of a body is such that every particle of the body moves uniformly in the same direction, it is called translatory motion.” It can be linear (along a straight line), random (along an irregular path), or circular (along a circle).

explain.title: Rotatory motion
explain.body: “If each point of a body moves around a fixed point (axis), the motion of this body is called rotatory motion.” An electric fan and a top are examples.

explain.title: Vibratory motion
explain.body: “When a body repeats its to and fro motion about a fixed position, the motion is called vibratory motion.” A swing is an example.

mistakes: Do not confuse circular motion along a circular path with rotatory motion around a fixed axis; use the movement described in the question.
Do not call every back-and-forth movement rotatory: repeated to-and-fro motion about a fixed position is vibratory motion.
Do not define random motion as simply changing direction; the textbook definition is movement along an irregular path.
When asked for types of motion, include examples as well as the names.
